An admissible choice: for each oriented edge $ij$, select either $p^+_{ij}$ or $p^-_{ij}$, and assign the opposite choice to edge $ji$.

So for each unordered pair $\{i,j\}$, we pick one of the two basis vectors for $p_{ij}$ (the polynomial on the edge from $i$ to $j$), and the other basis vector is assigned to $p_{ji}$.

For each vertex $i$, define $p_i = \prod_{j \neq i} p_{ij}$, the product of the chosen polynomials for all edges incident to $i$.

Since each $p_{ij}$ is a polynomial of degree at most 1, and there are $n-1$ edges incident to vertex $i$, $p_i$ is a polynomial of degree at most $n-1$.

The question: does there always exist an admissible choice such that $p_1, \ldots, p_n$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{C}$?

The space of polynomials of degree at most $n-1$ has dimension $n$. So $p_1, \ldots, p_n$ are $n$ vectors in an $n$-dimensional space, and they're linearly independent iff they span the space.
